state.intent: Add a visual comparison of official central-bank policy rates to the morning market map, next to existing rates/FX context.
state.existing: Next16/React19, dark/light tokens --accent --text --text-muted --border --panel; accessible SVG, source drawers, six instruments and daily/weekly/monthly; 390px phone. Reviewed news cards precede Treasury/liquidity/FX/CFTC charts. Official policy headlines already exist lower down.
state.data: Actual sources: Fed target lower/upper daily percent via FRED; ECB deposit facility daily series, currently2.50%; Bank of England daily Bank Rate, currently3.75%; Bank of Japan October30 saved primary decision, approximate overnight target1.25%, no comparable daily history in this connector. Fed range3.75-4.00. ECB latest actual observationNov3, BoE Oct30, FedNov2; date differences must remain visible. Historical ECB/BoE/Fed series are available; BoJ is a saved decision, not a daily quote.
constraints: Show Fed as a range, BoJ as approximately, ECB/BoE as levels with distinct definitions
Common numeric scale for comparison; allow future negative rates
Show each original observation/decision date and source access
Do not imply rate differences are an FX trade, inflation-adjusted stance or predicted policy move
No chart fabricated for BoJ and no smooth trend inferred across policy jumps
Keep existing consensus and source drawer patterns; stack on phones

policy_layout.instructions: Choose a visual layout that makes different rate definitions and asynchronous source dates understandable.

criteria.shared_rate_lanes: One panel with four labelled horizontal lanes on a common percent axis; Fed range, ECB/BoE points, approximate BoJ marker; numeric values, definition, source dates and inspect control per row. Optional dates/history in drawer.
criteria.four_step_cards: Four cards with current values and small step charts for US/ECB/UK; BoJ has its published decision only. Each card keeps dates and source access.
criteria.comparison_table: A compact table with bank, rate, definition, observed date and source link; no comparison graphic.
